A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CATP-LLM study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-C. Text and rendered-page comparisons reveal no material gaps.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original OpenCATP experiments, including baseline comparisons in Table 2 and ablation, sensitivity and model-size results in Table 3 and Figures 6-7.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original OpenCATP experimental outcomes in Tables 2-3 and Figures 6-7.

M1.justification: TPL encoding and CAORL's context augmentation, intermediate rewards, adaptive masking and decision-transformer training remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same sequential and non-sequential OpenCATP tasks, including OpenAGI-derived tasks and 24 constructed non-sequential tasks. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains zero-shot, few-shot and HuggingGPT comparisons using GPT-3.5/GPT-4, alongside Llama2-7B IFT and RLTF. Figure 6 also retains the same comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains the 69/18 sequential and 12/12 non-sequential training/test task splits, 40 inputs per task, evaluation metrics and model configurations. Appendix C's experimental settings also match.

E4.justification: Both retain the component ablations in Table 3, QoP-weight sensitivity in Figure 6, backbone-size analysis in Figure 7 and qualitative planning case study in Figure 1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The point-estimate reporting in Tables 2-3 and Figures 6-7 is unchanged.

E6.justification: The numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout. For example, Table 2 reports CATP-LLM QoP of 0.2605 for sequential planning and 0.1762 for non-sequential planning in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(5), the decision-transformer formulation in Appendix A and pricing definitions in Appendix B are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning TPL, CAORL and OpenCATP, and the same claims of advantages over GPT-powered planners.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning parallel execution, cost feedback and model size remain unchanged. The GPU-resource limitation on evaluating larger LLMs and the appendix discussion of dependency types are also retained.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a generic promise to publish CATP-LLM/OpenCATP code with a specific GitHub repository pointer and explicitly includes the dataset. Other implementation disclosures are unchanged. The PDFs do not establish actual resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 2, Table 1 and all 54 reference entries are retained. The ToolkenGPT attribution footnote is relocated within page 4 without changing its meaning; reference backlink page numbers merely track text reflow.

P1.justification: The abstract's final resource statement and the date stamp are edited. The scientific prose, terminology, section order and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The title changes from two lines to one, shifting Figure 1 and subsequent text upward. Early-page text reflows, and the page 4 attribution footnote fits within one column. Figure/table contents and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The specific repository pointer for the promised code and dataset makes the resource statement more actionable, while keeping the attribution footnote together modestly improves readability. These are limited documentation gains; scientific evidence is unchanged, and actual resource availability is not established by the PDFs.
